log.why: Knocking out the top candidate ompF (0.411 prior) can directly confirm it to high confidence or shift focus to lacZ.
E2 splits Ticket 2's prior nearly in half (0.394 vs 0.606) while Ticket 1 already has E4 incubating.
Knocking out lacZ splits the posterior nearly in half and will strongly confirm or refute the leading 0.538 hypothesis.
Testing 3 µM bisects the remaining probability mass (0.47 vs 0.53) and can strongly confirm the leading 3 µM hypothesis.
Testing 10 uM splits the posterior mass (0.61 vs 0.39) and utilizes a free incubator before publishing Ticket 1.
Posterior for lacZ is 0.929 after positive E1 readout, giving high expected value and freeing a ticket slot.
Testing 10 µM splits Ticket 3's prior probability nearly in half (0.461 vs 0.539) while starting incubation early.
Testing {araC, ompF} splits Ticket 4's prior 0.58/0.42 and starts incubation before we publish Ticket 2.
E3 cleanly splits hypotheses at or below 3 uM from 10 uM while leaving time to publish Ticket 2 next.
Ticket 2 has only 10 seconds left and strong 0.796 posterior support for 10 uM.
Test araC directly to split the two main candidates (araC 0.496 vs ompF 0.444) while leaving plenty of time to publish Ticket 3 next.
With 11s left, no new plate can finish before expiry, and 10 uM already has a strong 0.708 posterior.
Ticket 4 has only 12s left and ompF has a strong 0.795 posterior after E5 and E0 results.
E6 tests top candidates hisG and ftsZ (0.444 total mass) cleanly before Ticket 5's 29 s deadline.
Pairing E11 {hisG, recA, gyrA} with growing E6 {hisG, ftsZ} cleanly separates top candidates hisG, ftsZ, recA, and ompF before expiry.
With 7 seconds left in the round and 5 seconds on Ticket 5, ftsZ has a strong 0.760 posterior supported by E6 and E11.
